title: OTAS Capability Manifest
description: Machine-readable declaration of a token's base type, behaviors, and the policy/registry and metadata anchor it points to, so a counterparty's system can determine compatibility before transacting (whitepaper 5.2). Each behavior also records WHERE ITS DESCRIPTION CAME FROM, per the native/observed spectrum of 5.4: a natively mapped behavior is declared by the issuer against OTAS conventions; an observed one is inferred by tooling from on-chain facts and is only as reliable as what the chain exposes. How much corroboration an observed description needs before a counterparty relies on it is an open question in the draft, so this schema records the provenance and leaves the sufficiency judgment to the consumer.

chain_namespace.description: CAIP-2 style namespace, e.g. eip155, sui

asset_id.description: Contract address (EVM) / coin type (Sui) / mint (Solana) / token id (UTXO)

mapping.description: Where this manifest as a whole came from (5.4). native = issued to conform, described by the issuer against OTAS conventions; observed = inferred by tooling reading on-chain facts; mixed = some of each, as most real tokens will be.

anchor.description: An observed description is valid only as of the state it was read from.

code_hash.description: Guards against proxy upgrades invalidating the description

source.description: issuer-declared = the description originates with the issuer; chain-observed = tooling resolved it from on-chain state (interfaces implemented, registries and policies referenced, extensions enabled, capability objects held).

binding.description: Rail-native mechanism, e.g. 'ERC-3643 canTransfer', 'Sui PAS Policy<T> + approval witness', 'Sui PAS clawback_funds', 'Token-2022 transfer hook'

corroboration_ref.description: Optional URI/hash supporting an issuer-declared behavior that on-chain state cannot confirm. How much corroboration is enough is left open by the draft.

not_confirmable.description: Behaviors the issuer declares or the token may have that could NOT be confirmed from on-chain state alone. Naming them is the point: absent from this list is not the same as absent from the token, and off-chain enforcement can exist with nothing observable on-chain.

exclusions.description: Behavior pairs mutually exclusive on THIS rail (canonical example: Solana confidential transfers x transfer hooks, since a hook that reads the amount is incompatible with an encrypted amount).

policy_refs.description: e.g. the Sui PAS Policy<T> whose required approvals are readable before a request is submitted, or an ERC-3643 compliance/registry address

metadata_anchor.description: Content hash of the canonical off-chain core descriptor
